name: Jutland
notes: The Jydsk hest - Denmark's national draught horse, out of the local workhorses of the Jutland peninsula and organised into a studbook late in the nineteenth century. Suffolk Punch blood is in it, which is visible here in the pool as well as in the silhouette.

Flaxen chestnut is the whole player-facing identity: a red body with a cream-to-blond mane, tail and feather. Chestnut is near-led rather than fixed, because the deliberate twentieth-century selection that produced the modern 'national colour' did not erase the older bay and black horses.
The pale mane is flaxen and not cream. Cream is forced wild on purpose - a palomino Jutland would be the wrong horse, and the draft's own rationale says so.

Grey, roan and silver are historically recorded and are kept at a couple of percent each. Silver is the weakest of the three: it rests on secondary breed descriptions with no Jutland PMEL17 count behind it, and on a chestnut-led breed it is invisible most of the time it is carried.
A medium draught, not a giant. The size band is the cited 157-164 cm and lands below the Shire and the Percheron on purpose; the breed's mass is in its width, which is not modelled.

Managed sources only. The population fell under 300 horses in 1998 and Danish conservation work brought it back near 2,000 by 2016, which is a recovering national breed rather than anything a player should find running loose.
All disorders clear. No Jutland-specific carrier rate was located for any locus, and a heavy draught build is not on its own a licence to seed PSSM1.
Moderately cold tolerant for Danish winters - a northern farm horse, but a lowland maritime one, so not the near-fixed pool the Nordic mountain breeds carry.
The heavy mane and tail, the feathering, real pulling force, harness work and the conservation registry itself are none of them modelled.
